A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TS-Mamba work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 includes an additional appendix. The supplied contents support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TS-Mamba evaluations on REDS4, Vimeo-90K-T, and Vid4, including component and token-number ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and reports additional module comparisons, temporal-window experiments, RealVSR evaluation, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Trajectory generation, token selection, TSMA branches, temporal scanning, reconstruction, and both loss terms are retained. The new procedure notation and additional ablation variants do not establish a change to the proposed TS-Mamba method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on RealVSR, substantially extending coverage from synthetic BI/BD degradations to real-world video degradation. The original training and benchmark datasets remain. Set5, BSDS100, and Manga109 in Table 7 contain explicitly reproduced prior-paper results, not new TS-Mamba evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DFVSR, MIA-VSR, IART, VSRM, and the online adaptation VSRM*. Appendix comparisons additionally include MambaIR/MambaIRv2 variants, real-world and diffusion-based VSR methods, S2SVR, and EGVSR/RTSR. TAMambaIR has no completed REDS4 comparison and appears only in the separate prior-results table.

E3.justification: The original training budget, preprocessing, scale factor, hardware, and benchmark metrics remain unchanged. New experiments introduce ILNIQE/NRQM evaluation on RealVSR and temporal-window settings from T=3 to T=23. The latter also report different model sizes, so this is not documented as a fixed-size window-only comparison.

E4.justification: v2 adds TSMA replacements using DCN, FGDA, DA, and FDA (Table 4), temporal-window sensitivity (Table 5), a rotation failure case (Figure 6), and temporal-consistency profiles (Figure 13). Figure 5 adds qualitative evidence for the retained component ablations; the original Tables 2–3 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–3 are retained, including TS-Mamba's REDS4 result of 30.73/0.8727 and 112G MACs. v2 adds substantial new results, including VSRM* at 30.64/0.8701 on REDS4 and TS-Mamba at 32.54/5.161 ILNIQE/NRQM on RealVSR, plus new ablation and qualitative findings. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendix 7.1 add finite-case scan-elimination calculations and explicit elimination ranges, and correct v1's intra-window value labelled delta_inter=8 to delta_intra=8. The procedure notation itself is equivalent. The added analysis contains a discrepancy: left/right shifts have elimination 14 in the prose but 12 in Figure 9.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the first SSM-based online VSR model, trajectory-based token selection within Mamba, and shifted Hilbert scanning for spatial continuity. The abstract retains the same three-benchmark performance claim and over 22.7% MAC reduction; additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly attributes rotation failures to inaccurate trajectories and compensation. Appendix 7.2.2 explains weaker results against specialized real-world models through the absence of noise and complex degradations during training. These add concrete applicability qualifications, alongside further explanations of scan complementarity and efficiency trade-offs.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the generic GitHub placeholder with a specific TS-Mamba repository address, although availability is still phrased as a future promise. v2 also documents the online VSRM* adaptation. The core implementation, hardware, and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and 7.2.2 substantially expand positioning against Mamba image/video restoration, diffusion-based temporal modeling, and real-world and real-time SR. Added discussion of MambaIR, MambaIRv2, TAMambaIR, VSRM, and newer diffusion methods explicitly contrasts their aggregation and scanning designs with TS-Mamba.

P1.justification: Most of the original abstract, method, and experimental narrative is retained. v2 expands introductory and related-work explanations, introduces compact procedure notation, adds numbered sections and an organized appendix, and updates author and publication-header text. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column ICLR layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. Table 1 expands, Tables 4–11 are added, and new figures show ablations, failures, scan analyses, and temporal profiles. Figures 7 and 11 redisplay parts of the existing Figure 3 rather than introducing wholly new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The added online Mamba comparison, module and window experiments, and explicit failure and real-world limitations improve support and transparency for the retained method. However, reporting problems limit the gain: Figure 9 conflicts with the scan-analysis prose, and Table 10 gives VSRM 3.0M parameters versus 17.1M in Tables 1, 6, and 8. Several new comparison settings are also sparsely documented. The net improvement is useful but limited.
